newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha slumps as crude stumbles, supplies good.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha slumps as crude stumbles, supplies good.

text.p: NWE naphtha shed some more of its recent strength on Friday as weaker crude combined with good supplies exerted bearish pressure.
Naphtha was down by $6-8 a tonne.
A Dow spec 10,000 tonne cargo was heard offered at $210 cif NWE, but it was not clear whether the Donges 17,500 tonne cargo heard offered yesterday at $216.50 cif was still available.
"The market has come down since then," said one dealer.
Buyers were looking for as low as $205 cif NWE for February product and sub $200 for March delivery.
Supplies in northern Europe were judged to be high
because the recent naphtha/crude crack spread has been wide, encouraging refiners to produce naphtha.
The spread started to narrow this week to around $60 a tonne, $10 off last week's high, but still higher than the normal range of $30/$50 a tonne.
Some support was derived from Far East players active on NWE swaps because of high prices in Asia, but most dealers thought prices would ease next week as fundementals played a more important role.
"It has been squeezed up with was hitting liquidity," said one .
